Appealing as the idea of battling Cthulhu in a bullet hell shooter can be, I found [b]Project Starship[/b] too chaotic, not helped by the play area feeling very cramped. By the end of a run, you'll likely have to put a weight on the slow motion button because it's the only way for your eyes to make out anything. The graphics, besides being amateurish, are often unclear, with some enemies not standing out over backgrounds; near the end, the first time I didn't even realize I was inside some canyon and I was losing energy because I was crashing into the walls, also because there were no such obstacles beforehand. The random generation only results in levels that, even if lasting a few minutes each, feel too long for the little variety they offer.

I have to commend some bullet barrages that seem impassable at first sight but in truth have small spaces where you can maneuver with the small weak point of your ship, but really too little to save a game that can be nice for a few minutes of mindless shooting, before moving on to the many better shmup alternatives on Steam.

This is bar none one of the worst shmumps and or games I have ever played in my life period. It both looks and feels like a flash game, and until I read the description which explicitly states it's purely randomized I had no idea if the banal and utterly monotonous quality of my run was intentional or not. Turns out the RNG is just so poorly salted you can get what I got, which is a bootleg Touhou clone that's so barebones it doesn't even have a sound effect for your shot hitting enemies, let alone the enemies dying. The 'enemies' are 90% abstract blobs and shapes, the music loops continuously, the ship has the SLIGHTEST of inertia on movement, just there to make you question your sanity and then hate turning. And, lo and behold, to top it all off, there's a stage which introduces collision damage from terrain with NO indication what is the terrain or that it's a unique type of damage. I just assumed I was getting hit by invisible lasers until I realized what I thought were pre-fire laser indicators were actually THE BOUNDARY OF THE WALL I WAS SUPPOSEDLY 'FLYING INTO'. No bump or screen shake to indicate I was smashing into something, no distinction from a normal hit, and there goes a run where I have otherwise not been hit into instant oblivion. There is nothing of value here and I question the sanity of people who were able to enjoy playing this game.

>A Grandes Rasgos:
Pues... este titulo es un Shoot em up/Bullet Hell puro y duro~♥ como shmup tiene todo de estos: power ups, escuditos y una "bombini" y como bullet hell todo lo caótico de estos... incluido un apartado randomizer y tu puntito vital; es amigable con jugadores que no son asiduos al genero ya que tiene modo fácil donde puedes con un gatillo ralentizar el tiempo, para cuando la pantalla se llene de demasiados enemigos/balas y no mueres de un golpe; tienes 6 inicialmente que puedes "mejorar" o perder, ya que su parte feita (punto de vista personal) es su apartado "randomizer"/roguelike todas tus partidas serán diferentes y una mezcla de enemigos, niveles y power ups... lo único que no cambia son los bosses... así que... put0s roguelikes arruinaron los no roguelikes(?).

El Plot es el de todo shmup; salva al mundo de...ThucuLoh... que diga Cthutulujuju; podemos escoger a uno de 2 personajes, que no cambian mucho, mas que la estética y los sonidos de voz ingame.

>Lo Bueno:
+El Gameplay es solido, si amas los shmups/bullet hell una solida adquisición.
+La Banda Sonora es decente; no molesta y a la vez tiene beats bastante bonitos.
+La cantidad de power ups y enemigos es decente... menester mencionarlo ya que siendo un indie le echaron ganitas; que hay que enfatizar eso, ser un jugador a un creador  de jueguitos es muy diferente (hacer jueguitos es un infierno y jugarlos no tanto xD).
+La curva de dificultad/aprendizaje es buena; necesario decirlo: es un titulo difícil... pero justo, todo depende de que tanto quieras avanzarlo... lo que deriva en su aprendizaje y sorteo de obstáculos.

>Lo Malo:
-Put0s roguelikes los odio! ÒwÓ en este caso los power ups debes medirlos conforme a tu estilo de juego; hay power ups "trol" que en vez de ayudarte te pueden cambiar todo... así que prueba todos y memoriza que hace cada uno: el mas roto es el aim bot.
-Muchos mencionan su duración o de que es un "árcade" lo que es relativo a cada persona: si eres un chino que juega con sus bolas y se termina todos sus títulos en 20 minutos; pues obvio sera una tontada el titulo... de otra forma te dará buen gameplay en lo que aprendes y dominas el jueguito (ojo yo no lo he terminado, llego hasta un cuarto boss y en mis primeros 30 minutos no pasaba del segundo).
-Podría ser... el arte que bien es amateur... y se entiende; y aun así es decente; considera que es un indie, un titulo hecho por tal vez 3 tipos o menos.

Pues... si eres amante de los shoot em ups como io, es una solida compra 7/10, tomando en consideración que viene de un team pequeño de desarrolladores, de otra forma y si es que buscas algo mas elaborado, hay mejores opciones, sin menoscabo de la calidad de este titulo; que da una experiencia buena con tan poco presupuesto ojo que es un titulo difícil, y dominarlo es lo que le da gameplay.

I'm not going to pretend this game is perfect, because there are some not-insubstantial drawbacks.
The powerups that drop keep dropping after you're maxed out on the stat they would increase, the upgrades are incredibly unbalanced, with some being straight-up downgrades if grabbed at the wrong time, and at just about no point is what any of them do actually explained.
That said, somehow, it's still fun. Don't expect greatness from it, but you can do a lot worse.

A quaint little game going for a specific old school Japanese arcade game aesthetic. Clearly inspired by Raiden and similar vertical shooters.

It's not terrible but it feels overall unpolished and strange. The most off-putting aspect for me was the lack of sound effects for... most things, including enemies getting hit, the majority of enemy attacks, and the player getting hit or killed (although that does have musical distortion to indicate it). Also annoying is the lack of i-frames (and/or screen clearing) after getting hit, which is what you'd expect from most games of this type, and leads to a lot of fast drainage of your health.
The game is also a bit inconsistent with its visual and audio style, with some sprites being pretty clean while others appear intentionally limited (the character art in particular), and the fact that the game has many 8-bit style sound effects and compressed voice clips despite playing modern electronic music.
I will say that the music is actually surprisingly good, one of the best aspects of the game.

Again, the game is not horrible, it's clearly someone's passion project and of course it doesn't cost much at all. It is a serviceable cheap vertical shooter. But, I can't bring myself to play it for very long. It probably should have spent more time in the oven before it was served.

The sequel, Project Starship X, looks a heck of a lot better. I might try it out at some point.

TLDR: Bullet hell sections hard to dodge on small screens. Game progression hinges on snowballing powerups together. Game has uneven pacing of low and high points.

My experience with this game has been basically to put together the powerups until you mostly steamroll everything. Due to the setup I have here I know that sensitivity on gamepads are impacted by my small display. So I am not holding that against the game. Eventually that grinded me to death. Otherwise it felt like I could probably keep going for a fairly long time on easy difficulty without too much of an issue. Game offers a higher difficulty as well. The movents and aiming felt alright. However the camera did not have much field of vision, some screen real estate was wasted. Sound effects sometimes stopped were absent from one sequence to the next. The game also had inconsistent hitboxing, sometimes allowing to attack enemy bullets and sometimes having your fire go right through them, exposing you to real danger of dying and force you to dodge instead due to the unreliable implementation. 

In conclusion this game can probably offer plenty of entertainment for the dollard it asks. On the other hand, it is easily outcompeted by any well polished shootemup title and there is a lot of saturation in those on the Steam Market. This library entry is thus very redundant and hard to justify keeping in permanent library.

Очень напоминает Star Drifter от Back To Basics Gaming, только вот отзывы у "Дрифтера" почему-то заметно xуже. А так тот же жанр и сеттинг, такая же низкая цена, саундтрек тоже въедается в мозг, а простенький дизайн и имитация экрана старого телевизора вызывают ностальгию. И те же главные косяки: крошечное окошко, которое никак нельзя растянуть, не говоря уже о фулскрине, и множество эффектов, делающих ваши попытки уворачиваться от пуль еще более сложными. На телевизоре играть невозможно, да и за монитором некомфортно - маленькое окошко, слишком много мелких снарядов, которые очень просто не заметить из-за обилия эффектов. Хитбоксы тоже странные - порой кажется, снаряд попал, но нет, вот он пролетает мимо. А порой не пролетает. Не помогает и рандомное появление врагов со всякими mad events, во время которых на экране творится настоящий хаос. Если очень хочется сыграть во что-то подобное - купить за копейки на распродаже можно, но вряд ли игра вас затянет хотя бы на час, да и запомниться ей особо нечем. Я же, возможно, позже дам игре еще один шанс, но пока порекомендовать ее не могу.

P.S.: насчет полной поддержки геймпада наврали - вначале все равно придется пару раз щелкнуть по клавиатуре.
P.P.S.: идиотская автоцензура в Стиме теперь даже слово "xуже" заменяет сердечками, если написать его русскими буквами.
